aiReview.method: Development-time assistant review of every record in each deterministic, template-stratified review sample, including Gurmukhi, English and selected source senses. aiReview.sampling: Up to six evenly spaced distinct main-corpus slots per enabled template, excluding quoted-word practice. examples.originalEnglish: The cousin (maternal aunt's son) holds a school.
examples.fix: Fixed institutions/places fail the physical holding frame; choose a manipulable object.
Reject the sun-only rise binding for a human. The valid come-out sense remains a separate, currently unprofiled construction.

examples.gurmukhi: ਕੀ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਈਮੇਲ ਰੱਖ ਸਕਦੇ ਹੋ?
examples.roman: kī tusī̃ email rakkh sakde ho?
examples.fix: Digital content is distinct from a physical sheet; holding is rejected while digital keeping/storage remains allowed.
English money is singular mass: “There is money in Auckland.” Punjabi ਪੈਸੇ ਹਨ stays plural.

examples.originalEnglish: How many money do you need?
examples.fix: Use “How much money do you need?” while retaining Punjabi plural quantity agreement.
examples.observedSamePunjabiFinalEnglish: How much money do you need?

examples.gurmukhi: ਉਹ ਕਲਮ ਨਾਲ ਈਮੇਲ ਲਿਖਦਾ ਹੈ।
examples.roman: oh kalam nāl email likhdā hai.
examples.originalEnglish: He or she writes an email with the pen.
examples.fix: The writing instrument and medium must agree; choose a physical message/letter for a pen.
The nominal English gloss renown is not approved as a predicative adjective; retain the other valid senses and dictionary record.
Whose supplies the determiner: “Whose razor is this?”

examples.gurmukhi: ਦੇਵਰ ਪਤਝੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੁਕਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੇਜ਼ ਵੰਡਦੀ ਹੈ।
examples.roman: devar patjhaṛ vich dukān vich mez vaṇḍdī hai.
examples.originalEnglish: The brother-in-law distributes a table in the shop in autumn.
examples.fix: Use masculine agreement for devar; a single table uses the existing give-away alternative.

examples.gurmukhi: ਮਹਿਲ ਮੁੰਗਫਲੀ ਵੰਡਣੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਚਾਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
examples.roman: mahil muṅgphalī vaṇḍṇī nahī̃ chāhũdā hai.
examples.originalEnglish: The wife does not want to share peanut.
examples.fix: Peanut receives a singular count determiner. The uncommon wife sense remains explicitly uncertain rather than receiving an invented gender correction.
